current_fastest_Rust.scope: Fastest explicitly documented post-JSON timer including input preparation and worker creation/run/join. Artifact restoration and JSON IO are tracked in whole-process time.

scope.primary_resources: All-thread process counters and allocator requests inside complete post-JSON measurement windows
scope.managed: measurement field includes input admission/setup, native execution, worker create/run/join, internal cleanup and result materialization
scope.Rust: PROCESS_METRICS.processing; post-JSON eligible only when declared complete boundary includes all preparation and worker lifecycle
scope.preinitialized_Rust: PROCESS_METRICS.processing retained as excluded_processing; no comparison to managed complete post-JSON counters
scope.whole_process: Separate /usr/bin/time -lp counters from launch through exit, including restore, JSON IO, postJSON and final destruction
scope.RSS: Endpoint resident/footprint counters in each window; peak resident/footprint from whole process separately; allocator peak is not RSS
scope.allocation: Original allocator all-thread requested allocations/reallocations; freed bytes can include allocations predating the window; excludes allocator internals, OS stacks and mmap
scope.free_call_count_reason: Current measurement helper records freed bytes, not number of free calls
scope.restore: Managed restore_measurement kept separate; precompiled artifact restoration/validation, outside postJSON
scope.JSON: Managed json_measurement and Rust reported preparation window retained separately; never added to postJSON
scope.latency: Instrumented timings are diagnostic only; no speed/reference selection or goal completion is inferred here
scope.sizes: Ordinary and instrumented executable file/section sizes separate; native code/stack from checked compiler metadata where available
